key_insight: The paper argues that multiple disciplinary frameworks are converging toward a unified concept of "physical AI"—systems that combine embodiment, morphology, control and learning to act intelligently in the real world. It reframes embodied intelligence as an engineering-scientific agenda that requires hardware-software co-design and new evaluation metrics.
problem_solved: Clarifies and synthesizes disparate theories and approaches so researchers can move beyond simulation and cognition-only models to design, evaluate and build agents that physically interact and adapt in real-world environments.
method: Survey and synthesize frameworks from robotics, cognitive science, control theory and machine learning to define 'physical AI' and its core components.
Propose a conceptual taxonomy and research agenda emphasizing sensory-motor coupling, morphology-aware learning, hardware-software co-design, and sim-to-real transfer.
Illustrate with representative case studies and evaluation criteria that bridge simulation, benchmarks and real-world deployment.
impact: Provides a roadmap that helps AI/ML practitioners prioritize embodied system design choices (sensors, actuators, morphology, and learning algorithms) and adopt evaluation practices that reflect real-world performance and robustness. This shift enables more reliable sim-to-real transfer, safer deployment, and richer capabilities for autonomous agents.
visual_elements: A layered diagram showing components of Physical AI: morphology → sensors/actuators → control/learning → environment (with bidirectional arrows for sensorimotor loop).
Taxonomy infographic mapping disciplines (robotics, ML, control, cognitive science) to research priorities and methods.
Pipeline graphic for sim-to-real: simulation → domain randomization / learning → hardware-software co-design → real-world evaluation.
Comparison chart (table or icons) contrasting traditional 'cognition-only' AI vs embodied/physical AI across metrics like robustness, adaptability, and sample efficiency.
paper_title: From embodied intelligence to physical AI
